comment-1: Expected target/reference ratio per diagram, with tolerance. The workflow marks rows outside band in the summary; nothing fails. Update these deliberately when a change legitimately moves performance, in the same commit as the change (or the reference bump).
comment-2: Tolerance calibrated 2026-08-29 from 4 identical-engine (A/A) runs on 4 distinct runner CPU models (Xeon 8370C, EPYC 9V74, Xeon 6973P-C, EPYC 7763): worst observed A/A deviation was 0.07, most rows within 0.05. 0.10 sits above that noise floor while still flagging real regressions.
comment-3: Ratios centered 2026-09-06 on the per-diagram median of 3 perf-bench runs (Actions #32-#34, commit 9f92a3b, 3 distinct runner CPU models) against the new pin (npm:1.2026.8), which folds in P2-P5 so target/reference is back near 1.0. Worst deviation from these medians over those 3 runs is 0.14 (puml-1), 0.13 (puml-0), 0.10 (puml-19), the rest 0.08 or under - a thinner sample than the 11-run history behind the previous centering (worst 0.07 there), so treat puml-0/puml-1/puml-19 as provisional and revisit once more runs accumulate. Recenter on the same median rule whenever the pin moves.
